# Handoff: a way back to the JusPrin view from classic OrcaSlicer

Written 2026-10-27 for the agent who implements this. Untracked working note; never commit it. The design and the reasoning behind it are in `classic-view-return-design.md` (same folder, also untracked); this file is what to build. Branch: `jusprin-newui`.

## What this is

JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer whose production UI ("the shell") is installed over OrcaSlicer's MainFrame at startup by fork-owned code. The Prepare header's overflow menu has a row "Switch to classic view…" that uninstalls the shell in place and shows stock OrcaSlicer with the same project open. Today there is no way back in the same session; the person has to quit and relaunch. Build the way back.

## Decisions already made (Kenneth, 2026-10-27)

- **Two surfaces**, both fork-owned: a banner above OrcaSlicer's Notebook and a row in OrcaSlicer's View menu. Both re-install the shell.
- **Session-only.** Do not write the `jusprin_shell` config key. Relaunch is always JusPrin, as today.
- **Wording.** Banner text: "You're in the classic OrcaSlicer view." Banner button: "Back to JusPrin". Menu row: "Switch to JusPrin view". All through `_L()`.
- **Minimum design, default styles, no canvas boards.** Dress the banner with the existing recipes and palette only (`Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, `ShellTheme`): `style_label` with `text_secondary` for the sentence, `style_button` with the `secondary` button recipe for the button, `surface_canvas` background (the same as the StatusRow header; the secondary button hovers in `surface_subtle`, so a `surface_subtle` banner would hide its hover state), `border_subtle` bottom line, layout spacing on the 4/8/12/16 scale. Add no token and draw no board. If a value you need truly has no token, stop and ask rather than typing a literal.
- **Zero new lines in OrcaSlicer-owned files.** Everything below is reachable through public API from fork code. If you find yourself editing anything outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, stop and read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`; the design was chosen so you never need to.

## Where things are

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp`
  - `shell_slot()` (line 172): the static `unique_ptr<ShellController>` that holds the installed shell.
  - `ShellController::install` (263) and `uninstall` (1351). Install's preconditions: the Plater is page `tp3DEditor` of the Notebook, and the Notebook is an item of the main sizer. Uninstall restores both, so a fresh controller can install again.
  - `show_orca_calibration_menu` (1333): the precedent for editing OrcaSlicer's menus from fork code. macOS: `m_frame->GetMenuBar()` and `FindMenu(_L("Calibration"))`. Windows/Linux: `m_frame->topbar()`.
  - `attach_shell` (1597), `installed_shell` (1650), `detach_shell` (1655). `attach_shell` is called once from the MainFrame constructor (`src/slic3r/GUI/MainFrame.cpp:541`, the fork's one seam there) with the frame, the Notebook and the main sizer. It runs once-per-frame startup policy (update check, three `app_config` writes), then declines if `jusprin_shell == "0"`, then builds and installs a controller, logging on failure.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:499`: the "Switch to classic view…" row. It runs `frame->CallAfter([]{ detach_shell(); })` so the header's own handler returns before uninstall destroys the header. Mirror this timing on the way back.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/MainFrame.hpp:263`: `BBLTopbar* topbar()`, public. `src/slic3r/GUI/BBLTopbar.hpp`: `wxMenu* GetTopMenu()` is the title-bar dropdown on Windows and Linux; `MainFrame::init_menubar_as_editor` adds the View menu into it with `AddDropDownSubMenu(viewMenu, _L("View"))` (MainFrame.cpp:3287). On macOS the same `viewMenu` is appended to the `wxMenuBar` (MainFrame.cpp:3438). `MainFrame::m_main_sizer` is private; you already hold the pointer from `attach_shell`.
- `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`: the integration harness that runs the whole app. `--classic-switch` (flag parsed near line 11975) runs `verify_uninstall_restores_stock` (line 11571), which chooses the menu row and checks the stock presentation came back. `--stock` (near 11959) launches with `jusprin_shell: "0"` written into the run's config (near 12234). The header comment at the top of the file lists every flag and how the harness is run.
- `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, "Writing UI code": the rules for any fork surface. `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`, "Sibling widgets and static owners must plan for destruction order": why the controller binds the frame's `wxEVT_DESTROY` and abandons rather than restores on teardown. Your new controller lives in the same static slot pattern and needs the same care.

## What to build

### 1. `Shell/ClassicView.hpp/.cpp`: a fork-owned controller for classic view

One class, say `ClassicViewReturn`, constructed with the frame, the Notebook, the main sizer and the `ShellTheme`, plus a callback to run when the person asks to go back. `install()` and `uninstall()`, symmetric, like `ShellController`. Add the files to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` (note: a new file there re-runs CMake and forces a long rebuild; add both files before your first build and do not restart a running build).

**Banner.** A `wxPanel` inserted into the main sizer at the Notebook's index (`main_sizer->GetItem(tabpanel)` gives you the position; on Windows and Linux the BBLTopbar is above it and stays above). Horizontal sizer: the sentence on the left as a `wxStaticText`, the button on the right as an OrcaSlicer `Button` dressed with `style_button(..., metrics().button.secondary)`. Height: whatever the secondary recipe's height plus scale padding gives; do not pin a height. Not dismissible. Repaints on appearance change the way the shell's other panes do (`apply_current_appearance` in ShellController is the pattern). `uninstall()` detaches it from the sizer and destroys it.

**Menu row.** Find the View menu, append a separator and "Switch to JusPrin view", keep the item's id. macOS: `frame.GetMenuBar()->GetMenu(bar->FindMenu(_L("View")))`. Windows/Linux: walk `frame.topbar()->GetTopMenu()->GetMenuItems()` for the item whose label is `_L("View")` and take `GetSubMenu()`. A missing View menu is a thrown `std::runtime_error`, as the Calibration lookup throws; see "Failure" below for where it is caught. `uninstall()` deletes the row and the separator by id.

Both the button and the row call `frame.CallAfter(callback)`. Neither touches the shell directly.

### 2. Re-entry in ShellController.cpp

- Add a fork-owned static attach point beside `shell_slot()`: the frame, Notebook and main sizer `attach_shell` received. `attach_shell` fills it on its first call.
- Split `attach_shell`: keep the once-per-frame startup policy where it is; move "build a controller, install it, log on failure, put it in the slot" into a new `install_shell()` that returns whether it installed.
- New `reattach_shell()`: uninstall and drop the classic-view controller, then `install_shell()`. If that fails, put the classic-view controller back and tell the person with OrcaSlicer's `MessageDialog` (`src/slic3r/GUI/MsgDialog.hpp`; never `wxMessageBox`, Kenneth finds it ugly): "JusPrin's view couldn't be opened." with the logged reason as the second line.
- Install the classic-view controller in three places: at the end of `detach_shell()` after `uninstall()`; in `attach_shell` on the `jusprin_shell == "0"` early return; and in `attach_shell` when `install_shell()` fails. A second failure at retry time then reaches the dialog instead of silence.
- **Failure of the classic-view install itself.** Install the banner first, then the menu row. A thrown menu lookup is caught at that one boundary (the function that installs the classic-view controller), logged with `BOOST_LOG_TRIVIAL(error)`, and leaves the banner in place: the banner never depends on a menu, so the way back survives an upstream menu rename. Do not catch anything else.
- `installed_shell()` must keep returning `nullptr` in classic view; the preferences hook installed by the shell (`set_preferences_handler`, ShellController.cpp around line 790) already checks this.

### 3. What a round trip must preserve

- OrcaSlicer's project, plates, presets and undo history: the shell never touched them; do not add anything that does.
- The project chat: `ProjectPersistence::attach()` adopts the open project through its auxiliary data directory, so the new controller should land on the same managed project document. Prove it in the harness (below); if it does not hold, stop and report rather than patching around it.
- Autosave is off in classic view by design (uninstall drops it and resumes OrcaSlicer's backup). Nothing to do; just do not "fix" it.
- Pane widths and collapsed states reset. Accepted.

## Verification (required before calling it done)

Build on the shared Mac with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target shell_integration_harness -- -j4` after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`; one build at a time, never restart a build to change targets (AGENTS.md, "Building on a shared machine"). The harness bundle is `build/arm64/tests/shell/RelWithDebInfo/JusPrinShellHarness.app`; run its executable with an isolated data dir, never against the installed JusPrin.

Extend the existing `--classic-switch` run inside `verify_uninstall_restores_stock`, after today's checks:

1. Record the managed project id before the switch (`installed_shell()->persistence()->document().project_id()`).
2. Check the banner is shown and the View menu has the row.
3. Choose the menu row (reuse the harness's menu-driving helpers, or call `reattach_shell()` directly for the first pass if driving a native `wxMenu` is awkward; say which you did). Wait for `installed_shell() != nullptr`.
4. Re-run the installed-shell checks the harness already has at startup: tab strip hidden, sidebar unavailable, Prepare legacy overlays hidden, canvas wider than 200 px, Calibration menu off the bar (macOS), the project's chat has the same project id as step 1.
5. Check the banner and the row are gone.
6. Switch to classic again and go back through the banner button this time. Two full round trips, so a leaked binding or handler shows up (the Plater open handlers, the idle binding, `set_preferences_handler`, the frame's `wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK`).
7. In `--stock` mode (launches with the shell off): check the banner and row are present, go back, check the shell installed.

Also run the UI guards (`brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`) since you touched a fork surface, then look at the banner in the running app in light and dark appearance. The harness runs on the Mac only; the Windows title-bar dropdown needs one manual pass, or say plainly it was not run.

Report outcomes faithfully: failing checks with their output, anything skipped and why.

## Out of scope

- Persisting the choice across launches (`jusprin_shell` writes). Decided against for now.
- Any new token, canvas board, or design pass. Decided against.
- Reworking the overflow menu itself; that is `prepare-overflow-menu-proposal.md`, a separate change.
- Edits to OrcaSlicer-owned files. None are needed.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is

The fix is done but not committed, and the harness now passes. The default shell harness run prints `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0` and exits 0; `--classic-switch` and `--stock` also pass and exit 0. The changes are in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/classic-view-return-fix` on branch `claude/classic-view-return-fix`, cut from 9104408c92. The main checkout no longer has my edits.

**Why it took so long:** the builds were the problem, as you guessed. Other sessions committed to `jusprin-newui` in the shared checkout twice while I worked. Each new commit changes the commit hash compiled into every file, so each build recompiled about 780 steps instead of one file. Once I moved to the worktree, it needed one full build and then only quick rebuilds.

**Why the run stopped with no result:** the harness crashed with a segfault (exit 139). On the second switch to classic view, the switch ran while a web view the shell had just recreated was still setting up its script handler. Removing the shell then freed that web view mid-setup. This shows up when a switch comes right after a return, as it does in the harness.
- The fix in `ShellController.cpp`: `detach_shell()` now waits until that setup has finished before removing the shell, retrying every 50 ms. `GUI_App::run_wizard` and `PrinterPanel` already wait the same way.
- The harness's own exit hit the same crash, because it closed the window right after the shell came back through the banner. Its `finish()` now waits the same way before closing the frame.

**Why the draft and project id didn't survive (default run only):** the classic-view return code was fine. In the default run, the step just before replaces the project. The project chat's storage only picks that up on its next timer tick or workspace event. Meanwhile the harness recorded the old project's id and wrote the draft into the old project's chat. The new project replaced it a moment later, so the draft was lost. The harness now settles that pending replacement before it records the id, using the same public call the shell's timer makes.

Two things I haven't fixed or tested:
- **A possible bug in the return path (my hypothesis):** if someone switches to classic view inside that same short window after replacing a project, the handoff could pair the new project with the old project's conversation. I haven't reproduced it.
- **Leftover harness folders:** the runs I killed while debugging probably left data folders named `jusprin-shell-*` under `/var/folders/6y/fn1z996148dc7xjy2mxx5wkc0000gp/T/`. I didn't delete any because I can't tell them apart from other sessions' folders.
